verdict.rationale: Poly ships a `poly` CLI inside the desktop app. It is described as "scriptable from the terminal", runs commands against the local Poly app, and can create, update and organize files, so scripts can drive it from outside. The specific mechanisms the story names (URI scheme, deep links, or a documented local endpoint for opening notes in the app) are not evidenced. missing for 10: a URI scheme or deep links for creating/opening notes, a documented local HTTP endpoint, evidence that external calls can open a note in the app UI, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive the app from outside — create or open notes via a URI scheme, deep links, or a local endpoint — to wire it into my scripts and workflows

citations.quote: poly is Poly's command-line tool: your files, searchable and scriptable from the terminal. It ships inside the desktop app—there's no separate download.
teaches an agent how to search, read, create, update, and organize your Poly files by composing poly commands.
When Claude Code starts, the plugin runs poly memory summary against the local Poly app.
cp — Copy between local disk and Poly, or within Poly ... wget — Download a URL straight into Poly
